method: Wash and dry the lettuce and tomato. Shred the lettuce and slice the tomato; put both on a clean plate, separate from the raw filling.
Warm the wholemeal flatbread in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 30–60 seconds on each side, until flexible. Keep it covered on a clean plate.
Cut the chicken breast into strips about 1.5cm thick. After handling raw chicken breast, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat the measured olive oil in the non-stick frying pan. Cook the chicken strips over a medium-high heat for about 8–10 minutes, turning regularly so every side colours. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat and the juices are clear. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.

Put the measured katsu-style sauce into a small saucepan. Warm over a low heat, stirring, for about 2–3 minutes until bubbling and hot throughout; follow a longer cooking time on the sauce label. Keep warm for serving.
Put the lettuce and tomato on the warm flatbread. Add the cooked chicken strips and the warm sauce, fold the bread around the filling and serve immediately.

review.notes: Cooked white chicken breast strips with browned edges in folded unseeded wholemeal flatbread, shredded lettuce, sliced tomato and katsu-style sauce. No breadcrumb crust, cheese, mayo or herbs. Correct strip filling and one central serving.
